style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: tamasic pleasure deludes the self from start to finish
candidates.evidence: मोहनमात्मनः (deluding the self) / अग्रे च अनुबन्धे च (at first and in the end)

candidates.angle: sleep, laziness, and negligence as the source of tamasic pleasure
candidates.evidence: निद्रा-आलस्य-प्रमाद-उत्थम् (born of sleep, laziness, and negligence)

candidates.angle: Krishna names the lowest pleasure as tamasic

angle_en: Tamasic pleasure deludes the self from start to finish
angle_hi: तामस सुख आत्म को शुरू से अंत तक मोहित करता है

en.intro: Krishna finishes sorting the three kinds of pleasure. Listen to how he describes the lowest one.
en.notice: Krishna points to a pleasure born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, and says it deludes the self from the very beginning to the very end.
en.next: Krishna then reminds us that no being on earth is free from these three qualities.
en.meaning: That pleasure, born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, deludes the self at the beginning and at the end; it is called tamasic.

hi.intro: कृष्ण तीन प्रकार के सुखों का वर्णन पूरा करते हैं। सुनिए, वे सबसे निचले सुख को कैसे परिभाषित करते हैं।
hi.meaning: जो सुख निद्रा, आलस्य और प्रमाद से उत्पन्न होता है और जो आरम्भ और परिणाम में अपने आपको मोहित करता है, वह तामस कहा गया है।
hi.notice: कृष्ण यहाँ स्पष्ट करते हैं कि नींद, आलस्य और प्रमाद से पैदा होने वाला सुख व्यक्ति को शुरू से अंत तक भ्रमित करता रहता है, क्योंकि यह आत्मज्ञान को नष्ट कर देता है।
hi.next: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि पृथ्वी, स्वर्ग या देवों में कोई भी प्राणी प्रकृति से उत्पन्न इन तीनों गुणों से मुक्त नहीं है।

en.body: That pleasure, born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, deludes the self at the beginning and at the end; it is called tamasic. Krishna points to a pleasure born of sleep, laziness, and negligence, and says it deludes the self from the very beginning to the very end. Krishna then reminds us that no being on earth is free from these three qualities.
